# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout;
  keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under
  parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a
  single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way
  to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public
  restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent /
  `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry`
  and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb
  (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace
  `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration
  tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining
  core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals`
  and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the
shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview
when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each
apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and
the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated
  gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?**
  — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title
  and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
  (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?**
  — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is
  identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the
  description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level
  path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7
  behaviour is fully observable?**
  — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the
  default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require
  observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and
  demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the
  threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or
  a gym-local panel?**
  — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` /
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the
  shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the
  established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?**
  — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the
  gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence.
  Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic
  matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal
  relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.
data.title: Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').

- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

Raised during intake of AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (field pickups must upgrade temporarily). The producer asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* to represent consumable temporary grants (P6 Phase Shift charges, P7 Teleport stacks) whose unconsumed grants persist until consumed even after the temporary level window expires.

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.

## Summary
A reproducible evaluation harness: run the bot (and replay a human recording) on the same seed, produce metrics, A/B two bot versions, and render side-by-side clips. This is how we "re-run the bot production code" after changes.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A headless runner executes the bot for N ticks/seeds and emits a deterministic report (from telemetry).
- AC2: Same-seed comparison: bot vs human recording, and bot-vs-bot across versions, with metrics (survival time, minerals/min, power-ups, enemies/asteroids destroyed, avoidable hits, input cadence).
- AC3: A/B runner compares two bot configs/versions and reports the difference with confidence (multiple seeds).
- AC4: Optional side-by-side video via the existing capture tooling.
- AC5: Results are reproducible (same seed + config → same report) and stored as artifacts.
- AC6: Tests for the runner/report (pure aggregation) and determinism.
- AC7: Docs: how to run evaluations and interpret the report.

## Summary
Later phase: make the bot **match a player's style** using recorded telemetry (parameter fitting and/or behaviour cloning), on top of the competent framework.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: A pipeline that extracts style features from human recordings (reaction latency, hold distribution, target preferences, engagement distances, risk appetite).
- AC2: A parameter-fitting path that maps those features onto the structured bot's tunables (preferred first; keeps safety guarantees).
- AC3: (Optional/stretch) A behaviour-cloning policy trained from `(state → input)` pairs, evaluated against the structured bot on the same seeds.
- AC4: Evaluation shows the styled bot is measurably closer to the human recording than the default competent bot, without regressing competence/survival.
- AC5: Docs: how to train/fit and evaluate a style.
- AC6: Tests for the feature extraction (pure).

Depends on the recording/analysis tooling and the evaluation harness. Lower priority than competence.

# Intake Brief — Enhance Central AI boss encounter

**Work item:** Enhance Central AI boss encounter: 200 HP, more minions, figure-8 movement, top-screen health bar, hit feedback (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X)

## Problem statement

The Central AI boss encounter is currently a static, 400-hit grind: the boss does not move, the health bar is drawn relative to the boss container (so it is visibly displaced rather than at the top of the screen), and individual hits give no feedback beyond a bullet disappearing. Players cannot read their progress and the fight lacks the mobility and impact expected of a climactic boss. This work item reduces the boss's total health to **200**, reinforces the fight with **more minions**, gives the boss **figure-of-8 movement**, fixes the **health bar to the top of the screen**, and makes **every hit obvious through SFX and VFX**.

## Users

- **Player (primary):** fights the boss after clearing Level 5 and wants a readable, impactful, mobile encounter.
  - *As a player, I want to see the boss's health decrease with every hit so I know my shots are registering.*
  - *As a player, I want the fight to feel dynamic and dangerous, with the boss moving and more enemies on screen.*
  - *As a player, I want clear audio/visual feedback on each hit so the encounter feels responsive.*
- **Developer/maintainer (secondary):** wants the change implemented once in the shared core so the game and boss gyms stay in parity.
  - *As a developer, I want the boss behaviour to live in the shared core so `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` cannot diverge.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Boss total health is 200.** The boss spawns with 200 total hits across the existing **4 phases (50 hits per phase)**. The 4-phase structure, phase transitions, and score/minion rewards gated on *depleting* hits are preserved. Verified by unit tests: hit 49 stays in phase 1, hit 50 advances to phase 2, and hit 200 destroys the boss.
- **More minions are spawned with the boss.** Phase 1 spawns **12 scouts** (6 per side), phase 2 spawns **12 divers** (6 per side), phase 3 remains **0** (the pulse is the threat), and phase 4 spawns **15 swarm**. Verified by `BossMinions` unit tests asserting the per-phase counts via `minionCountForPhase`.
- **The boss moves in a figure-of-8 pattern.** The boss traces a lemniscate around its spawn anchor (≈120 px horizontal, ≈60 px vertical amplitude, ≈8 s per full cycle), staying within the playfield. Movement is implemented once in the shared boss/combat core and is identical in `PlayScene` and every boss gym. Hit detection continues to use the boss's live position, and the health bar does not move with it. Verified by tests asserting the traced position and bounded amplitude.
- **The health bar is fixed at the top of the screen and decreases per hit.** The bar is camera-fixed, horizontally centred at the top of the playfield, always visible during the encounter, and **not** offset or moved by the boss's figure-8 motion. Its fill shrinks proportionally on every hit (200 → 0) with the four phase-segment dividers retained. Verified by tests asserting the bar's screen position is independent of the boss position and that `getHpFraction()` decreases after hits.
- **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
- **Test coverage.** New/updated tests cover the health model, minion counts, figure-8 motion, health-bar placement, and hit feedback across `Boss.test.ts`, `BossMinions.test.ts`, `GymBoss.test.ts`, `PlayScene.test.ts`, and the audio cue contract.
- **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, the Game Design Document (§4.3), `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§5.1 parity), and the audio cue mapping/manifest.
- **Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (mandatory):** gameplay behaviour must live in the shared core (`src/scenes/core/`, `src/entities/`) and be consumed by both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss`; no divergent copies. The `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` duplicate-body guard and gym-parity docs assertion must still pass.
- **Preserve the 4-phase model:** do not change the phase attack patterns, telegraphs, or reward gating; only retune totals/counts and add movement/feedback.
- **Health bar model:** keep the existing proportional `getHpFraction()` fill and the four phase-segment dividers.
- **Audio pipeline:** a new SFX cue must be registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` and `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` (the contract test enforces completeness).
- **No new dependencies.**
- Stay within the existing visual/neon style and UK-English documentation conventions.

## Existing state

# Add 10% weighting to owned upgrades in hold-full choice

## Problem statement

When the hold fills and the player is offered a choice of upgrades, owned upgrades (weapon-level / power-up-level options) should appear 10% more likely than they currently do. Currently all candidates are selected uniformly at random; owned upgrades should receive a 1.1× weight multiplier.

## Users

- **Player (progression):** "As a player, when offered a hold-full choice I want a reasonable chance of upgrading an upgradeable weapon or power-up I already own, so my build keeps improving rather than forcing me to chase new items."
- **Designer:** "As a designer, I want owned upgrades to appear 10% more often so progression feels steady across runs."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — 10% weighting.** Owned level-up offers (both `weapon-level` and `power-up-level`) have a 1.1× weight multiplier applied during candidate selection. Unowned (base-pool) items retain 1.0× weight.
- **AC2 — Single source of truth.** The weighting logic lives in the strategy layer (`createRandomChoiceStrategy`), not in `buildChoiceCandidates`; no duplicate weighting code in scenes or gyms.
- **AC3 — Gym↔game parity.** The behaviour is identical in `PlayScene` and every gym that opens the hold-full choice, because they share `MineralChoiceScene` and `powerups/choice`.
- **AC4 — Configurable weight.** The 1.1× multiplier is a named constant (e.g. `OWNED_UPGRADE_BONUS_WEIGHT = 1.1`) so it can be tuned later without hunting for magic numbers.
- **AC5 — Testing/validation.** Unit tests verify: (a) owned-level candidates receive 1.1× weight; (b) weighted random selection produces the expected distribution (10,000 trials, ±3% tolerance, owned items appear ~10% more often than unowned items relative to pool size); (c) gym↔game parity tests pass.
- **AC6 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes. (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour must live once and be consumed by both the game and every gym.
- **Backward compatible:** no breaking changes to the `ChoiceStrategy` interface or existing `ChoiceOption` consumers.
- **No gameplay logic changes beyond weighting:** the candidate list itself is unchanged — only the selection probabilities shift.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — add weighting logic in `createRandomChoiceStrategy`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymMinerals.ts` — no changes expected (they already pass context).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/choice.test.ts` — new tests for weighted selection (10k trials, ±3%).
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MineralChoiceScene.test.ts` — parity tests.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR** — Show upgrade change summary and New badge in the hold-full choice list (completed).
- **AH-0MUPMPCB2009J54J** — Weapon leveling (completed).
- **AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q** — Asteroids drop collectable minerals that fill the ship'\''s hold (completed).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Statistical testing (low):** proving 10% bias requires many trials; tests use 10,000 draws with ±3% tolerance band.
- **Scope creep (low):** adding per-weight tunability (player-facing weight editor) could expand scope. Mitigation: this item implements a single constant only; per-weight tuning is a separate chore if needed.
- **Assumption:** "10% more likely" means a 1.1× multiplicative weight, not an additive 10 percentage points.
- **Assumption:** "owned upgrade" means `weapon-level` and `power-up-level` kind options in the candidate list.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Scope of owned upgrades?** (A: both weapon-level and power-up-level; B: only weapon-level; C: both with different weights.) — Answer (Producer): A — both weapon-level and power-up-level.
- **Q2 — Where does weighting logic live?** (A: in `buildChoiceCandidates` with tagged weights; B: in `createRandomChoiceStrategy` strategy layer.) — Answer (Producer): B — in the strategy layer.
- **Q3 — Test tolerance for statistical validation?** (A: 10,000 trials, ±3%; B: 50,000 trials, ±1%; C: 5,000 trials, ±5%.) — Answer (Producer): A — 10,000 trials, ±3%.

# Intake Brief — Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old

## Problem statement

AI_Hell's enemy roster (E1–E7) is a coherent but self-contained set of
formations. It does not yet deliberately mine the **classic arcade era** for
signature, instantly-recognisable enemy behaviours. This epic researches that
era and turns the best candidates into implementable work items, so the game
can grow a distinctive "arcade homage" roster without ad-hoc, un-scoped enemy
requests.

## Users

- **As the game designer**, I want a researched, curated catalogue of classic
  arcade enemy behaviours adapted to AI_Hell's neon-vector rules, so that new
  enemy work starts from a clear design brief rather than a one-line wish.
- **As an implementing agent/developer**, I want each selected enemy to have
  its own work item with a user story, testable ACs, predicted key files and a
  plan that follows the existing data-driven enemy convention, so I can
  implement it without re-deriving the design.
- **As the producer**, I want the candidates that were considered but not
  selected recorded, so the roster can be expanded later without redoing the
  research.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A research document exists at `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` that
   catalogues **at least 5 and at most 8 selected** classic arcade enemy
   archetypes. For each it records: source game, the original behaviour,
   how it is adapted to AI_Hell's rules (neon-vector, code-drawn, no
   enemy–enemy collision), and why it was selected.
2. The research document includes a **"considered but not selected"** section
   listing the remaining candidates from the research pool, each with a
   one-line reason for deferral, so the range can be expanded later.
3. **One child work item exists per selected archetype**, each containing a
   user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria (including unit tests),
   predicted key files, and a plan that follows §8.6 "Adding a new enemy" in
   `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`. Each child references this epic
   and the research document.
4. Each selected archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven
   pipeline — i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or
   needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` + factory/fire-dispatch seam — and give
   its **enemy difficulty scoring** inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
5. Each selected archetype's notes name the **gym scene(s)** that will exercise
   it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) to satisfy the gym↔game parity rule.
6. Validation: the research document's recommendations are checked against the
   existing engine constraints (every selected archetype maps to an existing or
   explicitly-planned formation/shot-pattern registry entry), and every child
   work item carries explicit unit-test acceptance criteria.
7. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** — no external art assets
  (GDD §7.2).
- **Gym↔game parity** — an enabled gameplay object must run the same code in a
  gym and the game; shared behaviour lives in `src/scenes/core/`. Enforced by
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs
  assertion (AGENTS.md).
- **Data-driven enemies** — tuning is data, not code; archetypes are rows in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN). A genuinely new entity is
  only justified when the existing formation/shot registries cannot express it.
- **"Enemies are the bullets" design** (GDD §2.4) and **no enemy–enemy
  collisions** (GDD §2.6).
- **Behaviours must be adaptable to a top-down free-2D arena** — the original
  arcade games are lane/axis-based; the brief must state how each archetype is
  translated (or note where translation is not faithful).
- **Scope is research + design + child-item creation.** This epic does not
  itself implement the enemies; each selected archetype's implementation is its
  own child work item.

## Existing state

- **Enemy catalog** (GDD §4.1, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §1):
  E1 Scout, E2 Diver, E3 Tank, E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, E6 Asteroid, E7 Harvester,
  plus the multi-phase Boss.
- **Enemy implementation guide** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`
  documents the shared core scene library, the CSV pipeline (§8), and the
  "adding a new enemy" checklist (§8.6).
- **Data-driven pipeline**: `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`, `src/core/configTypes.ts`,
  `src/core/configDefaults.ts`, `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`,
  `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts`, `src/entities/enemyFire.ts`,
  `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts`, `src/utils/formations.ts`.
- **Difficulty scoring**: `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` (absolute 0–100 index;
  movement/fire/health factors), pinned by
  `src/waves/enemyDifficulty.campaign.test.ts`.
- **Gym surface**: single reusable `GymEnemies` scene + `GymIndex`; new CSV rows
  appear automatically.
- **Precedent**: E6 Asteroid (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) is already an arcade homage
  built as a non-formation roamer with a split helper — a model for how far a
  new archetype may depart from the formation model.
- GDD §8 "Future Scope" already anticipates "Levels 6–10+ with new enemy
  types".

## Desired change

Produce researched, ready-to-implement enemy concepts drawn from classic arcade
games and capture each as a scoped child work item, with a shared research
document acting as the catalogue and the record of deferred candidates.

**Proposed candidate pool** (research selects 5–8; the rest go in the
"considered but not selected" section):

- Space Invaders — marching row that steps left/right and drops bombs.
- Galaga — entrance dive-in formation and tractor/capture beam.
- Pac-Man — ghost chase with distinct pursue/ambush personalities.
- Centipede — segmented chain that descends and reacts on segment destruction.
- Defender — fast attacker with a defined patrol/attack run.
- Missile Command — incoming falling projectiles / orbital strike telegraphed.
- Robotron 2084 — aggressive horde that swarm-steers toward the player.
- Frogger — lane traffic hazard crossing the arena (non-shooting obstacle).
- Joust — flapping momentum-based flyer in the top-down arena.
- Dig Dug — burrower that creates/changes traversal hazards.
- Q*bert — diagonal hopper with a fixed stepping pattern.
- Star Castle — concentric rotating ring shielding a core.

*(Every candidate in the pool is recorded in the research document; only 5–8
become child work items.)*

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` — New. The catalogue of selected and
  deferred archetypes (the epic's primary deliverable).
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — Updated. Add a reference to the
  research doc; each implemented archetype later updates the catalog (§1) via
  its child item.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Updated. Reference the research doc from
  §4.1 / §8 so the roster direction is traceable.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — Updated (by child items, not this epic). New
  rows for archetypes expressible as data.
- `src/entities/<Name>.ts` — New (by child items). Only for archetypes needing
  new entity code (e.g. burrower, segmented chain).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` / new gym scene — Exercised by child items for
  parity.

## Related work

- **Enemy Design tooling** (AH-0MTFP7EIC004F1MN) — completed; the data-driven
  CSV pipeline new enemies plug into.
- **Asteroids as an enemy** (AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F) — completed; precedent for a
  classic-arcade-inspired, non-formation enemy.
- **Enemy difficulty scoring** (AH-0MTZWZ7MC002B01K) — completed; every new
  archetype must supply its scoring inputs.
- **Extract common enemy base class for regular enemies** (AH-0MU4KQ6NT006MP52)
  — completed; the `BaseEnemy` seam new archetypes extend.
- **Data-driven enemy health config** (AH-0MUJRVYJH00485YR) — completed.
- **Docs and README for enemy config pipeline** (AH-0MTHG5K6O008BCNJ) —
  completed.
- **Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide**
  (AH-0MTAN4X5D009D7U6) — completed; the guide §8.6 governs each child.
- **Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic** (AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ) —
  completed; automated playtests must survive any new enemy, so its behaviours
  are a useful validation input for selected archetypes.
- **Alternative player control** (AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD) — completed.
- **Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments**
  (AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY) — completed; docs-update conventions to follow.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ** – Smart capture bot: survival-first heuristic that seeks power-ups and minerals and dodges fire patterns (completed)
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** – Alternative player control (completed)
- **AH-0MUE2MIXB007VOCY** – Documentation: README, ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION, code comments (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: classic, create, drawn, dropping, eats (+23 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: arcade, classic, create, drawn, dropping (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: create, enemies, epic, era, etc (+17 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the research could expand indefinitely. Mitigation — cap
  selection at 5–8 this round; record all other candidates in the deferred
  section. Extra opportunities become linked work items, not scope.
- **Fidelity risk**: lane/axis-based arcade behaviours may need significant
  translation to the top-down free-2D arena; the brief requires each archetype
  to state its translation, and permits a documented divergence (per gym-parity
  rule).
- **Pipeline-fit risk**: some archetypes (burrower, segmented chain) cannot be
  expressed as a CSV row alone; the brief requires each to state whether a new
  entity/factory seam is needed before implementation starts.
- **Assumption**: the operator-supplied exemplars (Space Invaders row,
  Pac-Man ghosts, Centipede) are illustrative examples, not a required final
  selection.
- **Assumption**: "classic arcade era" means the coin-op era of the late 1970s
  to mid-1980s.
- **Assumption**: this epic's children implement the enemies; no separate
  implementation epic is needed.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "How many enemy concepts should this epic research and turn into work
  items?" — Answer (operator): **(A) focused set of ~5–8** from a named
  shortlist of classics. Source: interactive reply. Research: reviewed
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §8.6 and the existing 7-archetype
  roster; a 5–8 cap keeps the epic tractable and each child implementable.
- Q2 "Should the epic also produce a written research/design document, or only

# Intake Brief — Bot is more gentle on the thrusters (AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A)

## Problem statement

The attract/demo bot's human-like thrust layer holds every forward-thrust press
for a fixed random band (200–225 ms normally, up to 400 ms on a long-travel
leg). This makes the bot's thruster "on" runs a little longer than a human's
and contributes to a slightly mechanical, over-eager feel. The producer wants
the bot to be a little gentler on the thrusters by shortening each press's
**on** time by a random **1–5%**.

## Users

- **Attract-mode viewer / operator:** watches the demo run and perceives the
  bot as a believable human pilot rather than a thruster-abusing machine.
- **Gameplay designers:** tune bot feel through one shared module without
  hunting for magic numbers.

Example user stories:

- *As an operator watching the attract demo, I want the bot to make slightly
  shorter, less mechanical thrust bursts, so that the demo reads as human play.*
- *As a designer, I want the gentle-thrust reduction to be a single documented
  tunable pair, so that I can adjust the feel without touching the governor
  logic.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Each forward-thrust press duration is reduced by a random factor drawn
  uniformly from **1%–5%** (inclusive of the configured bounds). With the
  default caps this shortens a normal press from the 200–225 ms band to
  ≈190–222.75 ms and a long-travel press from the 400 ms cap to ≈380 ms;
  unit-tested.
- AC2: The reduction is drawn **per press** and is reproducible for a given
  governor seed (a run-seeded governor produces an identical reduction
  sequence across two instances with the same seed); unit-tested.
- AC3: Continuous desired thrust still holds the thruster **on** for every tick
  (the reduction must not introduce off-gaps); existing continuous-thrust test
  remains green.
- AC4: The reduction bounds live in the shared `BotHumanInputTunables` module
  (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`) as documented min/max percent tunables with
  defaults `0.01`/`0.05`; no scattered magic numbers.
- AC5: Documentation is updated to describe the gentler thrust — the demo-bot
  subsection in `docs/Game Design Document.md` and the `botHumanLike.ts`
  module doc both note the 1–5% random reduction of press "on" time.
- AC6: At least one new automated test validates the reduction band and
  per-press randomness; full project test suite, typecheck and build must pass
  with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
  code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- AC8: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Keep the change surgical: only the thrust-press duration draw is affected;
  the chosen heading/target, reaction cadence, W/A/D key limits, and
  forward-model braking reflex are unchanged.
- No new dependency; keep the deterministic mulberry32 RNG already used for
  per-press jitter (do not introduce `Math.random()`).
- The reduction must be a *reduction only* (never extend a press), so the bot
  becomes gentler, not more aggressive.
- Single source of truth for tunables (`BOT_HUMAN_INPUT_TUNABLES`).

## Existing state

`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` implements the human-like input governor. In
`BotInputGovernor.resolveThrustPress`, a new press duration is drawn as:

```ts
const maxMs = longTravel ? thrustPressMaxMsLong : thrustPressMaxMs;
const span = Math.max(0, maxMs - thrustPressMinMs);
this.thrustPressRemainingMs = thrustPressMinMs + this.random() * span;
```

Defaults: `thrustPressMinMs: 200`, `thrustPressMaxMs: 225`,
`thrustPressMaxMsLong: 400`. The drawn duration is the thruster's "on" time.
`resolveThrustPress` is unit-tested in `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`
(`human-like thrust presses (AC15/AC16)` suite), and the GDD demo-bot
subsection documents the 200–225 / 400 ms bands.

## Desired change

After drawing the base press duration, apply a per-press random reduction of
1–5%:

```ts
const baseMs = thrustPressMinMs + this.random() * span;
const reduction =
  thrustPressGentleMinPct +
  this.random() * (thrustPressGentleMaxPct - thrustPressGentleMinPct);
this.thrustPressRemainingMs = baseMs * (1 - reduction);
```

Add the two bounds to `BotHumanInputTunables` and

## Goal

As a producer, I want `npm run capture` to record multiple gameplay clips in a single invocation, so that collecting a batch of N clips does not require an external bash loop that re-boots the Vite dev server, re-warms the game and re-installs Playwright bookkeeping on every iteration.

## Context

`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (see `package.json` script `capture`) currently records exactly **one** clip per invocation. The output path defaults to `capture-output/gameplay-<ISO-timestamp>.webm` (ms precision) or an explicit `--output`. There is no `--count`/`-n` flag.

Current workaround is a shell loop:

```bash
for i in {1..50}; do npm run capture || break; done
```

This works but is slow (each run boots its own dev server, warmup, then a full run + tail) and cannot reuse a kept server (`--keep-server`) across iterations cleanly.

## Expected behaviour

- New flag `--count <n>` with alias `-n <n>`, defaulting to `1` (preserving existing behaviour).
- The script performs `n` capture iterations in one process, reusing the dev server and browser resources where practical.
- Each iteration writes its own file; when `--output` is not supplied, continue using the timestamped default naming and guarantee uniqueness across iterations (e.g. include the iteration index / suffix, since same-ms timestamps collide within a tight loop).
- When `--output` **is** supplied with `--count > 1`, either reject the combination with a clear error or infer an indexed suffix (`demo-1.webm`, `demo-2.webm`, ...) — pick one and document it in `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the script's usage comment.
- `--scripted`, `--scenario`, `--tail`, `--max-duration`, `--warmup` apply to every iteration.
- `--json` reports one result object per iteration (or an array) with the produced files/probes.
- A failure in one iteration must be attributable: the summary must name the failing iteration, and the exit code must be non-zero (document whether later iterations are skipped or continued).

## Suggested implementation approach

- Extend `parseCaptureArgs` (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`) with `--count`/`-n`, validated as a positive integer.
- Wrap the existing single-capture flow in an iteration loop that keeps the server/browser alive between iterations where safe (reload rather than relaunch, if the run-end signal allows).
- Extend the output-path resolver to always produce unique names for multi-iteration runs.
- Update `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` and the script header usage block.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `npm run capture -- --count 3` produces 3 distinct non-trivial `.webm` files in `capture-output/` and exits 0.
- [ ] `-n` is accepted as an alias for `--count`.
- [ ] Omitting `--count` behaves exactly as today (single clip).
- [ ] `--count` with a non-positive / non-numeric value fails fast with a clear message and non-zero exit code.
- [ ] Multi-iteration runs reuse a single dev server (no repeated boot per iteration) — verified by log/probe evidence or a test.
- [ ] `--output` + `--count > 1` behaviour is deterministic, documented and covered by a test.
- [ ] `--json` output reports per-iteration results including file paths.
- [ ] `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` documents `--count`/`-n` and the output-naming rules.
- [ ] Unit tests cover arg parsing (default, valid, invalid, alias) and the multi-output path resolver.

# Add a reverse thruster to the Asteroids ship control scheme — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Under the shipped **Asteroids** control scheme the ship can only thrust *forward* (W / ↑) and turn (A / ←, D / →): there is no way to slow or back away while holding a heading. Players must spin the whole ship around to change speed. We want a **reverse thruster** — a held retro-thrust opposite the ship's facing direction, bound to **S / ↓** — that is individually tunable and can be switched off completely.

## Users

- **Player** (primary): needs an intuitive way to brake/back up without turning the ship, with the ability to disable the extra control if they prefer classic Asteroids handling.
- **Developer / designer**: needs to tune the reverse thruster (or turn it off) from the Player gym and persist it with the rest of the ship config.

Example user stories:

- As a player, holding **S / ↓** while flying forward decelerates my ship (retro-thrust) and, if held, accelerates me backwards in the direction opposite my nose.
- As a player who dislikes the reverse thruster, I can switch it **off completely** so S / ↓ do nothing and my handling matches the classic scheme.
- As a designer, I can tune the reverse acceleration and reverse max speed independently of the forward values, live in the Player gym, and see the ship's nose retro-thruster flame while reversing.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Reverse input & physics (Asteroids scheme only).** Under the Asteroids scheme, holding **S** or **↓** applies continuous acceleration **opposite** the ship's facing direction at a configurable reverse acceleration; releasing the key restores the normal friction behaviour. When no reverse key is held the ship behaves exactly as today. The 4-directional scheme is unchanged.
2. **AC2 — Individually customisable & persisted.** Reverse thrust is configured through `ShipConfig` with a master **on/off boolean** plus dedicated tunables — a **reverse thrust acceleration** and a **reverse max speed** — independent of the forward `thrustAcceleration` / `maxSpeed` values. The values round-trip through `src/data/ship-config.csv` and the config store, with sane defaults for legacy configs that predate the fields.
3. **AC3 — Can be turned off completely.** When the reverse toggle is disabled, S / ↓ produce **no** reverse acceleration, **no** reverse flame and no other movement side effect; forward thrust and turning are unaffected.
4. **AC4 — Reverse VFX.** Reverse thrust renders a dedicated forward-facing **nose retro-thruster** flame that grows/decays using the existing animated-flame model and rotates with the hull; only engines that are firing are drawn.
5. **AC5 — Gym control.** The Player gym exposes the on/off toggle and the reverse tunables (checkbox + sliders), applies changes live, and persists them via the existing Save path.
6. **AC6 — Demo bot unaffected.** The human-like demo governor continues never to emit reverse input (W/A/D only); `AsteroidsInput.reverse` is always `false` from the bot.
7. **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated (at minimum the GDD controls table and §2.2 movement, plus code comments), including a note that the reverse thruster exists, its default binding and how to disable it.
8. **AC8 — Tests.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes, and new/updated tests cover: reverse physics (acceleration, clamp, friction on release), the disabled-toggle no-op, config/CSV round-trip and legacy defaults, engine-selection/VFX for reverse, input mapping for S/↓, and the bot never emitting reverse.

## Constraints

- Applies to the **Asteroids** control scheme only (`controlScheme: 'asteroids'`); the 4-directional scheme already has a down/backward thrust and must not change.
- Must preserve **gym↔game parity**: reverse physics and VFX live in the shared core (`src/utils/movementModel.ts` + `src/entities/Player.ts`) and are consumed identically by the game and gyms — no divergent copy.
- Must be **backward compatible** with existing persisted `ShipConfig` / `ship-config.csv` data (missing fields fall back to defaults).
- **Depends on** the separate Teleport-automation item AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC: once Teleport is automatic, S / ↓ are free for reverse thrust and the manual-teleport key handling is removed.

## Existing state

- **Scheme/input:** `AsteroidsInputHandler.mapInput` (`src/utils/movementModel.ts`) maps W/↑ → `forward`, A/← → `turnLeft`, D/→ → `turnRight`; **S/↓ are deliberately excluded** (S is a 4-directional backward-thrust binding only).
- **Model:** `AsteroidsModel.tick` applies forward acceleration along `facing`, friction when `!forward`, a `maxSpeed` clamp and edge wrap. There is no reverse acceleration.
- **Engines/VFX:** `Player._engines()` defines the Asteroids engines `main` (rear), `leftSide`, `rightSide`; `getEngineActivity` returns them for forward/turn input, and `Player._updateFlames` animates each. No nose/retro engine exists.
- **Config:** `ShipConfig` (`src/core/configTypes.ts`) holds `thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `frictionDeceleration`, `controlScheme`, and the `asteroidsRotation*` fields; defaults in `src/core/configDefaults.ts`; CSV codec + `SHIP_COLUMN_ORDER` in `src/core/csv.ts`; shipped values in `src/data/ship-config.csv`.
- **Gym:** `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` renders one slider per numeric field (`SLIDER_RANGES`) with live apply + Save; there is no boolean/checkbox control yet.
- **Teleport conflict:** S (the `layerDrop` binding) and a hardcoded ↓ fallback currently activate a stored Teleport on key-down (`CombatScene._handleTeleport`). This is being removed by AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC (Teleport becomes automatic like Phase Shift), which this item depends on.

## Desired change

- Add `reverse: boolean` to `AsteroidsInput`; have `AsteroidsInputHandler` read **S** and **↓** for it.
- In `AsteroidsModel`, when reverse is held **and** the reverse thruster is enabled, apply `-cos(facing) * reverseAcceleration * dt` / `-sin(facing) * reverseAcceleration * dt`; gate friction on "no forward and no reverse input"; keep the existing clamp/wrap.
- Clamp the speed reachable under reverse thrust to the configurable **reverse max speed** — without abruptly braking pre-existing faster forward momentum (exact clamp semantics pinned by a unit test).
- Add a `nose` (retro) engine port to the Asteroids engine layout that fires when reversing, with an animated flame consistent with the other engines.
- Extend `ShipConfig` + defaults + CSV codec + `ship-config.csv` with `asteroidsReverseEnabled` (boolean), `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed`.
- Add the toggle + sliders to `GymPlayer` and cover the new behaviour with tests.
- Update the GDD (§2.2 movement, controls table) and code comments.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/movementModel.ts` — add `reverse` to `AsteroidsInput`; map S/↓ in `AsteroidsInputHandler`; apply reverse acceleration + clamp in `AsteroidsModel.tick`; return the nose engine from `getEngineActivity`; gate on the config toggle.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — add the `nose` retro-thruster `EnginePortDef` to the Asteroids layout and its flame rendering/animation.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` — add the three new `ShipConfig` fields.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` — default `asteroidsReverseEnabled`, `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration`, `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed`.
- `src/core/csv.ts` — extend `SHIP_COLUMN_ORDER`, parse/serialise/validate the boolean and numbers.
- `src/data/ship-config.csv` — add the new columns/values to the shipped row.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — add the on/off checkbox and reverse sliders (and their ranges).
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — keep `reverse: false` in the emitted `AsteroidsInput` (and the frozen idle input).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — controls table + §2.2 movement update.
- Tests — `src/utils/movementModel.test.ts`, `src/entities/Player.test.ts`, `src/core/csv.test.ts` / `configDefaults.test.ts` / `configStore*.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.test.ts`, `src/ai/botHumanLike.test.ts`, `src/scenes/demoMode.integration.test.ts`, and the parity guards `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` / `gymParityDocs.test.ts` if they assert the input shape.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** — Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift (free S / Down for reverse thrust) — **dependency (blocks this item)**.
- **AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD** — Alternative player control (introduced the Asteroids scheme, `AsteroidsInput`, engine layout).
- **AH-0MTFORPJ2003RWWQ** — Asteroids directional VFX improvements (key-specific engine selection: forward→main, turn→side).
- **AH-0MUNS42NA000N41U** — More precise turn controls (the closed-form angular ramp in `AsteroidsModel`).
- **AH-0MUX2NENC008AHOQ / AH-0MUXXQ1MN002RXGB** — Demo bot uses the ship's asteroid controls and is limited to human-like W/A/D.
- **AH-0MTFOSOHN001Q620** — Player thruster SFX (`getEngineSoundLevel`); check reverse interacts sensibly with the hum.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: key-map conflict (mitigated).** S/↓ previously activated Teleport. Mitigated by making Teleport automatic in the prerequisite item; this item owns S/↓ only once that lands.
- **Risk: reverse clamp could feel like sudden braking.** Applying a reverse-specific speed cap to pre-existing faster forward momentum would jerk the ship. Mitigation: clamp only the reverse-accelerated speed (or use the larger of current speed / cap) and pin the semantics with a unit test.
- **Risk: config-shape churn.** Adding fields to `ShipConfig`/CSV touches many tests. Mitigation: default-merge for legacy configs and update the CSV codec + fixtures together.
- **Risk: parity divergence.** A reverse implementation written only in `PlayScene` would break the gym↔game duplicate-body guard. Mitigation: implement once in the shared model/Player and consume from both.
- **Assumption:** "individually customisable" means the reverse thruster has its own tunables and master toggle, separate from forward thrust (operator chose option A).
- **Assumption:** the reverse thruster is **enabled by default** (the toggle exists to switch it off); shipping it on gives the feature immediate effect while preserving an opt-out.
- **Assumption:** reverse is Asteroids-scheme only; the 4-directional scheme is untouched.
- **Assumption:** the demo bot keeps its human-like W/A/D governor and never emits reverse (no objection raised; can be revisited).
- **Scope-creep note:** analogue reverse, reverse-specific SFX, or a reverse-auto-brake assist were noted but excluded; capture as new work items if wanted rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (intake agent) — How should the S / ↓ conflict with the manual Teleport activation be resolved?**
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** Do not overload the key. Create a **separate work item** to make Teleport **automatic like Phase Shift**, which removes the conflict, and make *this* item **dependent on that one**.
  — **Action:** created **AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC** ("Make Teleport automatic like Phase Shift") and added a dependency edge `AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG depends-on AH-0MUZE4AIP009HZWC`. The S/↓ (moveDown) binding is therefore owned exclusively by the reverse thruster.

- **Q2 (intake agent) — What does "individually customisable" + "turn it off completely" cover?**
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **A** — a persisted master `asteroidsReverseEnabled` **toggle** (with a Gym checkbox to switch it off completely) **plus** dedicated reverse tunables (reverse thrust acceleration and reverse max speed), independent of the forward-thrust values.

- **Q3 (intake agent) — How should reverse thrust be represented visually?**
  — **Answer (operator, interactive reply):** **A** — a dedicated forward-facing **nose retro-thruster** port that fires when reversing (exhaust shoots forward), distinct from the rear main engine; flames rotate with the hull.

- **Assumptions (raised with the operator; not disputed):**
  - Reverse is added to the **Asteroids** scheme only (4-directional already has backward thrust).
  - The demo bot keeps its human-like **W/A/D-only** governor and will **not** emit reverse.

## Goal

Make the stored **Teleport** power-up activate **automatically**, the same way **Phase Shift** already does, instead of requiring a manual **S / ↓** key press. This removes the S / ↓ key conflict that blocks the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG) and frees S / ↓ for held reverse thrust.

## User story

As a player, when a hostile threat closes in and I hold a stored Teleport, I want the teleport to fire automatically (like Phase Shift) so I am not required to reach for a key in the middle of dodging — and so movement keys are never overloaded with a consumable ability.

## Background / existing state

- **Phase Shift already auto-triggers** through the shared, single code path: `CombatScene._updatePhaseShiftAutoTrigger(dt)` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`) calls the pure `isInDanger(player, bodies, bullets)` helper (`src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts`; danger when the combined hostile-threat count within `DANGER_RADIUS` is >= 3) and feeds the result to `EffectsRegistry.updateDanger(inDanger, dt)` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`). The registry handles charge availability, re-arm-on-danger-cleared and a post-trigger cooldown, and plays the Phase Shift cue on activation. Every combat scene (game + gyms) calls this once per frame.
- **Teleport is manual:** `CombatScene._handleTeleport()` fires on `JustDown(teleportKey)` or the hardcoded ↓ fallback and calls `triggerTeleport()`, which consumes one stored Teleport stack (FIFO) and warps the player to the nearest safe spot along the heading, granting Phase Shift on arrival. Documented in GDD §4.4 / controls table as **S / ↓**.

## Expected behaviour

- Teleport auto-activates when the player is **in danger** (same danger definition/feed as Phase Shift) **and** a stored Teleport charge exists **and** the re-arm conditions are met (danger cleared since last trigger, cooldown elapsed) — mirroring the Phase Shift auto-trigger contract.
- Manual S / ↓ activation is **removed**; S / ↓ becomes available for the reverse thruster (AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG).
- Teleport keeps its existing trigger path: nearest safe spot in the direction of travel, consuming one FIFO stack, granting Phase Shift on arrival, and the existing Phase Shift activation cue plays.
- One shared implementation in the combat core so the game and every gym behave identically (gym↔game parity).

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — to be finalised by this item's own intake)

1. Teleport auto-activates via the shared danger feed when the ship is in danger, a Teleport stack is available, and the re-arm conditions (danger cleared + cooldown) are satisfied.
2. No manual S / ↓ (or `layerDrop`) activation of Teleport remains in the game or gyms; the ↓ fallback key is removed.
3. A stored Teleport is consumed exactly once per activation; stacking/FIFO semantics are unchanged.
4. The trigger uses the existing safe-spot + Phase Shift-on-arrival path; game and gyms share one implementation (gym↔game parity).
5. The re-arm/cooldown behaviour matches the documented Phase Shift model.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the change (GDD controls table, §4.4, any UI/HUD hints, code comments) — including the removal of S / ↓ for teleport.
7. Full project test suite passes with the new changes, with new/updated tests covering the auto-trigger, re-arm, and no-manual-key contracts.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — replace `_handleTeleport`/`teleportKey`/`downKey` with an automatic trigger fed by the shared danger feed.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — add Teleport auto-trigger state (charge check, re-arm, cooldown) alongside the Phase Shift model.
- `src/powerups/dangerDetection.ts` — reused as-is (shared danger signal).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` / `src/scenes/gym/*` — remove manual key wiring; ensure the shared auto-trigger runs.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — update the controls table and §4.4.
- Tests: `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, `src/scenes/RebindableControls.test.ts`.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Risk:** auto-teleport may fire more often than a player wants (each stored teleport is precious). Mitigation: match the Phase Shift re-arm/cooldown contract and make the trigger threshold explicit and testable.
- **Assumption:** "like Phase Shift" means the same danger-based auto-trigger model (not a timer), and the manual binding is removed entirely.
- **Blocker for:** AH-0MUZCSB4B00107RG (reverse thruster on S / ↓).

## Problem

Running `npm run build` from a git worktree created by the implement skill fails at the `build-audio` step:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'tsx' imported from /home/rgardler/projects/AI_Hell/node_modules/toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js
```

## Root cause

`scripts/build-audio.mjs` `resolveToneForge()` resolves the sibling checkout as `join(repoRoot, '..', 'ToneForge')`. Inside a worktree (`.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-<slug>`) that path is `.worklog/worktrees/ToneForge`, which does not exist, so resolution falls through to `tf` on PATH (`node_modules/.bin/tf -> ../toneforge/bin/dev-cli.js`). That copy has no `tsx` dependency, so the CLI crashes.

When built from the main checkout the sibling path resolves correctly and the build succeeds.

## Workaround used

`TONEFORGE_CLI=/home/rgardler/projects/ToneForge/bin/dev-cli.js npm run build` (the sibling's `node_modules` has `tsx`).

## Expected behaviour

`npm run build` succeeds inside a worktree without requiring `TONEFORGE_CLI` to be set manually, since worktrees are the mandated implementation workflow.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `npm run build` succeeds from a worktree with no `TONEFORGE_CLI` set.
- AC2: Sibling resolution is anchored to the main checkout (e.g. via the git common dir) rather than the worktree root.

## Summary

During a `dev`→`main` release (`/skill:ship release`), the audit-readiness gate's conservative in-gate remediation re-runs `audit_runner.py issue <id>` for a top-level `in_review` item whose stored audit is stale/missing/transient. For an item with a passing verdict the runner sets `needsProducerReview=yes` (by design, so the producer-review gate blocks until a human reviews).

The problem: if the item was **already producer-approved** (`needsProducerReview=false`) — the normal steady state after the producer has reviewed it — a content-unchanged re-audit nonetheless flips the flag back to `true` and immediately blocks the release at the producer-review gate (exit 9) and the final-validation sweep (exit 12).

## Example User Story

As a producer running a release, having already reviewed and approved every top-level work item, I want the release's automatic audit remediation not to re-open producer review for an item whose content I already approved, so that a stale audit does not silently re-block an otherwise shippable release.

## Observed

Release run on 2026-10-08 (AI_Hell, dev→main, v0.1.10 candidate):

- Item `AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1` (top-level `test-failure`, completed/in_review) had `needsProducerReview=false` for its **entire** recorded history (verified from the `refs/worklog/data` sync commits: false from creation 10:19 through the last pre-release sync at 11:16:27 UTC).
- The audit gate reported `auto-remediating AH-0MUZDXF2U001MJW1 (stale audit)` and `auto-remediated successfully` at 11:20:39 UTC.
- The producer-review gate then blocked with exit 9: `1 of 24 work item(s) need producer review`.
- `wl audit-show` confirms the fresh audit is green (`readyToClose: true`, content fingerprint unchanged).

## Expected Behaviour (candidate)

One or both of:

1. In-gate remediation should preserve an existing `needsProducerReview=false` approval when the item's content fingerprint is unchanged across the re-audit (only a genuine content change should re-open producer review); and/or
2. The producer-review gate should recognise a flag that was set by an in-gate remediation in the same run and not treat it as a fresh, un-reviewed requirement (e.g. compare against the pre-run approved state).

## Evidence / References

- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (in-gate remediation re-runs the audit; "the gate never calls wl update directly").
- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/audit-remediation.js` (bounded remediation; no flag preservation).
- `$(skill_path audit)/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~L11784: sets `--needs-producer-review yes` for top-level passing audits).
- Related: AH-0MUFGUYFC001A2OB (producer-review remediation hint flag casing).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A release whose only producer-review blocker is a flag set by the same run's in-gate audit remediation (item previously approved, content unchanged) does not fail the producer-review gate; verified by a unit test with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/remediation boundaries.
2. If an item's content genuinely changed since its last audit, re-audit still re-opens producer review (the safety behaviour is preserved); verified by a unit test.
3. No regression in the existing producer-review gate tests (child override/escalation, `null`/`undefined` handling).
4. Documentation (ship skill reference) states whether a content-unchanged re-audit preserves the producer-review approval.

## Summary

During the v0.1.10 dev→main release, the ship skill's **non-blocking** post-release branch cleanup (run-release.js step 10, `runPostReleaseCleanup`) failed:

```
Post-release cleanup: enumerating branches...
  ⚠ Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.
Found 0 merged local branch(es) to clean up.
Post-release cleanup: pruning local branches...
  Pruned 0 local branch(es).
Post-release cleanup: pruning remote branches...
  ⚠ Remote branch pruning failed: delete_remote_branches.py failed
```

Re-running the same scripts manually immediately afterwards succeeded (`summarize_branches.py ~6s`, `delete_remote_branches.py ~6s`, both exit 0), so the failure is not a permanent environment problem.

## Likely Cause

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a **fixed** report path `${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json` (`run-release.js` ~L735). In a multi-agent environment (herdr) where more than one agent may run a release/cleanup concurrently, the fixed path races: one process can truncate/replace the file while another reads it, producing the "Failed to read summarize report" path, and the follow-on remote prune inherits the broken state.

## Expected Behaviour

- The post-release cleanup uses a unique temporary report path (e.g. `mkdtempSync`) so concurrent runs cannot clobber each other.
- A transient cleanup failure is retried once, and the warning names the deterministic remediation.

## Evidence / References

- `$(skill_path ship)/scripts/run-release.js` `runPostReleaseCleanup` (fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json`; `delete_remote_branches.py` invocation).
- `$(skill_path cleanup)/scripts/{summarize_branches,prune_local_branches,delete_remote_branches}.py` — all succeed standalone.
- Discovered during release v0.1.10 (`discovered-from:release-v0.1.10`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a unique temp path per run; a unit test with two concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py`/report read no longer silently reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct, actionable warning.
3. The cleanup remains non-blocking (never changes the release exit code).

# Add a GitHub link to the main menu

## Problem statement

Players and contributors have no way to discover the project's source code from the game itself.

## Users

- **Player/Contributor:** Sees the game on-screen, wants to find the repo to report bugs, contribute, or learn more.
- **Reviewer/Tester:** Needs quick access to the source during code reviews or gameplay testing.

### User stories

- *As a player who enjoys the game, I can click/tap a visible link on the main menu to open the GitHub repository in a new browser tab, without losing my game session.*
- *As a keyboard user, I can Tab to the GitHub link on the main menu and press Enter to open it.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Renders:** A GitHub link (`🐙  GitHub`) is rendered as text in the bottom-left corner of the main menu (`MenuScene`), below the subtitle and at the same Y position as the subtitle. It uses the existing `MENU_TEXT_COLOR` (#00ffff) with the same padding scheme as other buttons.
2. **AC2 — Click opens repo:** Pointer-down on the link opens `https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell` in a new browser tab (`_blank`) with `noopener,noreferrer` flags.
3. **AC3 — Keyboard-accessible:** The link is registered with `FocusManager` after the Leaderboard button (Tab order: Play Game → Watch Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → **GitHub** → Gym Scene Index). Enter/Space on the focused link triggers the same action as a pointer click. Hover highlights the text in `#88ffff` (matching the existing pointer-over pattern).
4. **AC4 — Constant:** The URL is a single exported `const GITHUB_REPO_URL = 'https://github.com/SorraTheOrc/AI_Hell'` in `src/core/constants.ts` (re-exported from `MenuScene` for testability), used as both the display label and the click target.
5. **AC5 — Tests:** Unit tests verify (a) the button renders with the correct label, (b) pointer activation calls `window.open` with the correct URL and target, and (c) keyboard activation via `FocusManager.handleKey` triggers the same `window.open` call.

## Constraints

- **Keyboard parity (GDD §2.1):** No mouse is ever required. The link must be in the Tab cycle.
- **No mouse required:** Use Phaser's existing pointer + keyboard interaction model; no DOM overlay.
- **New tab only:** Always use `_blank` to preserve the game session.
- **Existing pattern:** Must match the visual style of other menu buttons (neon-cyan text, dark background padding).
- **No `FocusManager` changes:** Reuse the existing manager; do not modify its public API.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` renders 5 controls: Play Game, Watch Demo, Settings, Leaderboard, Gym Scene Index (dev, bottom-right, fixed position).
- All 5 controls use `this.add.text()` with the same visual pattern (fontFamily: monospace, 20px, MENU_TEXT_COLOR, dark background padding).
- A shared `FocusManager` (`src/utils/focusManager.ts`) handles Tab/arrow cycling and Enter/Space activation.
- `window.open` has not been used in `src/` before; Phaser's canvas is the sole rendering surface.

## Desired change

Add a 6th control (`🐙  GitHub`) to the main menu:
- **Position:** Bottom-left, aligned near the bottom edge (X ≈ 16, Y ≈ GAME_HEIGHT − 12), matching the Gym Scene Index button's offset pattern.
- **Activation:** `window.open(GITHUB_REPO_URL, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')` on both pointer and keyboard activation.
- **Tab order:** Between Leaderboard and Gym Scene Index.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Add the GitHub button (render, pointer handler, FocusManager registration).
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Export `GITHUB_REPO_URL`.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts` — Add tests for the new button.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Popup blocker:** `window.open` must be called synchronously within the user-gesture event handler; otherwise the browser may block it. Mitigated by calling `window.open` directly in the pointer/keyboard handlers.
- **Tab order change:** Adds a 6th control to the existing 5. The order (Play → Demo → Settings → Leaderboard → GitHub → Gym Index) follows visual hierarchy (top→bottom, left→right).
- **Hardcoded URL:** The repo URL is a constant, not environment-configurable. Acceptable for a personal project; fork maintainers would edit the constant.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: Where should the GitHub link live, and should it be keyboard-focusable? — Answer (operator): **A** — footer link, bottom-left, pointer-clickable and keyboard-focusable, appended to the Tab cycle. **Recommended** — keeps the GDD keyboard-parity contract intact.
- Q: How should activation behave? — Answer (operator): **A** — open in a new browser tab via `window.open(url, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`. **Recommended** — preserves the game session.
- Q: Where should the URL come from? — Answer (operator): **A** — single exported constant (`GITHUB_REPO_URL` in `src/core/constants.ts`), used for both label and click target. **Recommended** — testable, single source of truth.

## Related work

- **MenuScene Settings button** (AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N) — Similar pattern of adding a button to MenuScene.
- **In-game menu keyboard support (PauseScene)** (AH-0MUBZUQBL0080B88) — Keyboard navigation convention.
- **Add published game URL to top of README** (AH-0MUK3HYC3001YU05) — Same project URL, different location.
- **Create Main Menu scene** (AH-0MU72YVFR005VB2N) — Parent menu work.
